title: DR1's "Help with commodity codes" explains what a commodity code is and links to the Trade Tariff tool; the frontend's holds one sentence and no link.

finding.frontend: The details component on the commodity page has the same summary text as DR1 — "Help with commodity codes" — and one sentence inside it: "Commodity codes are used to classify goods for import and export." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:7-10). A user who does not know their commodity code is given no way to find one.
finding.prototype: The same disclosure carries three paragraphs: that commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers, that a commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods, and that the user can look them up using the Trade Tariff tool, linked to gov.uk/trade-tariff and marked as opening in a new tab (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:119-131).
finding.difference: Replace the single sentence in the commodity-codes disclosure with DR1's three paragraphs, including the Trade Tariff link and its "(opens in a new tab)" marker. The copy currently sits as a plain string in the feature's copy module, so it has to become markup or a paragraph list to carry a link.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a Trade Tariff link, or any commodity-code lookup route, anywhere else on the frontend's commodity page.
